controls.name: Network Segmentation
controls.objective: Networks must be segmented to limit lateral movement and contain the blast radius of security incidents. Systems must be grouped by trust level, function, and data sensitivity.
controls.description: Implement network segmentation controls to separate systems based on sensitivity, function, and trust level. Define security zones and enforce traffic filtering between zones using firewalls or network access controls.
key_requirements: Define security zones (e.g., DMZ, internal, management, production, development)
Enforce deny-by-default traffic policy between zones
Restrict inter-zone traffic to business-required flows only
Document and approve all cross-zone communication rules

controls.name: Network Traffic Filtering
controls.objective: Network traffic must be controlled and filtered based on least privilege principles. Only explicitly authorized traffic flows should be permitted; all other traffic must be denied by default.
controls.description: Deploy and configure firewalls, network access controls, and packet filtering to enforce traffic policies. Rules must be specific, documented, approved, and reviewed regularly to remove stale or overly permissive entries.
key_requirements: Enforce deny-by-default on all network boundaries
Restrict rules to specific source/destination/service combinations
Prohibit any-any-any allow rules without documented exception
Review and recertify firewall rules on a defined schedule
Remove or disable unused and stale rules

controls.name: Intrusion Detection and Prevention
controls.objective: Threats and anomalous network activity must be detected and blocked in real time. Security inspection must be applied to network traffic at all critical boundaries.
controls.description: Deploy IDS/IPS capabilities and attach threat prevention security profiles (antivirus, anti-spyware, vulnerability protection, URL filtering) to enforce security inspection on all relevant traffic flows.
key_requirements: Attach threat prevention profiles to all security policy rules
Enable antivirus, anti-spyware, and vulnerability protection profiles
Enable URL filtering on outbound traffic
Configure IPS/IDS signatures and alert on high-severity events
Review threat log alerts regularly

controls.name: Network Monitoring
controls.objective: Network activity must be continuously monitored to detect anomalies, unauthorized access, and security incidents. Traffic logs must provide a complete audit trail.
controls.description: Enable comprehensive traffic, threat, and system logging on all network security devices. Forward logs to a centralized SIEM for correlation, alerting, and retention.
key_requirements: Enable traffic logging on all security policy rules
Enable threat logging and forward to SIEM
Retain logs for a minimum period aligned with regulatory requirements
Alert on high-severity threat events within defined SLA

controls.name: Privileged Account Management
controls.objective: Privileged accounts must be tightly controlled, minimized in count, and subject to enhanced authentication and monitoring to prevent unauthorized administrative access.
controls.description: Enforce strict controls on privileged accounts including administrator accounts on network devices. Limit the number of local admin accounts, enforce role-based access control (RBAC), and monitor all privileged activity.
key_requirements: Minimize the number of local privileged accounts
Enforce role-based access with least privilege
Disable default or shared administrative accounts
Log and audit all privileged account activity
Review privileged account assignments periodically

controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.objective: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) must be enforced for all privileged access, remote access, and access to critical systems to prevent credential-based attacks.
controls.description: Require MFA for administrator logins to network devices, remote management access, and VPN connections. MFA must be enforced at the authentication profile level and cannot be bypassed.
key_requirements: Enforce MFA for all administrator accounts on network devices
Enforce MFA for remote access (VPN, SSH, HTTPS management)
Configure authentication profiles with RADIUS/LDAP + OTP or certificate
Disable password-only authentication for privileged access

controls.name: Access Review
controls.objective: User and account access rights must be reviewed and recertified at regular intervals to ensure that access remains appropriate and that stale accounts are revoked.
controls.description: Conduct periodic access reviews for all accounts including administrator accounts on network devices. Review admin roles, authentication settings, and VPN user accounts. Revoke access for terminated or role-changed personnel.
key_requirements: Conduct quarterly or semi-annual access reviews for admin accounts
Revoke access for inactive or terminated users within defined SLA
Document access review results and approvals
Validate that assigned roles align with current job function

controls.name: Security Event Logging
controls.objective: Security-relevant events must be logged with sufficient detail to support incident investigation, forensic analysis, and compliance reporting.
controls.description: Configure all security-relevant systems to generate logs for authentication events, configuration changes, policy matches, and threat detections. Logs must include timestamps, source/destination, action, and outcome.
key_requirements: Log all authentication events (success and failure)
Log all configuration changes with committer identity
Log all security policy matches and actions
Log all detected threats with severity and action
Include source IP, destination IP, port, protocol in traffic logs

controls.name: Log Retention
controls.objective: Security logs must be retained for a sufficient period to support forensic investigation, regulatory compliance, and audit requirements.
controls.description: Establish and enforce log retention policies that meet regulatory and business requirements. Logs must be stored securely and protected from tampering. Minimum retention periods typically range from 90 days to 1 year or more depending on regulation.
key_requirements: Retain security logs for a minimum of 90 days online and 1 year archived
Protect log integrity — logs must be immutable once written
Forward logs to a centralized, secure log management platform
Regularly verify that logging is active and logs are flowing

controls.name: Baseline Configuration
controls.objective: All systems must be configured according to approved security baselines and hardening standards. Deviations from baseline must be documented and approved.
controls.description: Develop and maintain approved baseline configurations for all network devices based on industry benchmarks (CIS, DISA STIG, vendor security guides). Configurations must be documented, version-controlled, and applied consistently.
key_requirements: Define and document approved baseline configuration for each device type
Apply CIS or vendor hardening benchmarks
Disable unused services, ports, and management interfaces
Enforce secure TLS/SSL profiles and cipher suites
Disable weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithms

controls.name: Configuration Change Control
controls.objective: All changes to system configurations must be controlled, authorized, tested, and documented before implementation to prevent unauthorized modifications and configuration drift.
controls.description: Enforce a change management process for all configuration changes to network devices. Changes must be raised as formal change requests, reviewed and approved, tested where possible, and linked to a change ticket in the ITSM system.
key_requirements: All configuration changes must be authorized via change management process
Changes must reference an approved change ticket
Commit logs must capture the committer identity and timestamp
Emergency changes must be reviewed within 24 hours of implementation
Configuration backups must be taken before changes

controls.name: Configuration Hardening
controls.objective: Network devices must be hardened to reduce attack surface. Unnecessary services, protocols, and features must be disabled. Strong authentication and encryption must be enforced.
controls.description: Apply hardening controls to eliminate unnecessary attack surface on network devices. Disable unused management interfaces, enforce secure management protocols (HTTPS, SSH), configure strong password policies, and restrict management access to approved IP ranges.
key_requirements: Restrict management interface access to approved management networks only
Disable insecure management protocols (Telnet, HTTP)
Enforce strong password complexity and rotation policies
Disable unused features and services
Apply strong TLS profile with approved cipher suites

controls.name: Change Authorization
controls.objective: All changes to production systems must be formally authorized before implementation. Unauthorized changes must be detected and reversed.
controls.description: Require formal approval for all changes to network device configurations. The change management process must include risk assessment, approval by an appropriate authority, and a rollback plan. Unauthorized changes must be detected through configuration monitoring.
key_requirements: All changes must be formally approved before implementation
Change records must document approver, scope, and business justification
Changes outside the approved window must trigger an incident
Configuration drift from approved baseline must be detected and remediated

controls.name: Vulnerability Management
controls.objective: Vulnerabilities in systems must be identified, assessed, and remediated in a timely manner based on risk severity.
controls.description: Conduct regular vulnerability assessments of network devices. Monitor vendor security advisories and apply patches within defined SLA. High-severity vulnerabilities must be remediated with priority.
key_requirements: Conduct vulnerability assessments at least quarterly
Monitor vendor security advisories for critical patches
Remediate critical vulnerabilities within 30 days, high within 60 days
Document vulnerability findings and remediation status

controls.name: Encryption Standards
controls.objective: Cryptographic algorithms and protocols must meet current security standards. Weak or deprecated algorithms must be prohibited.
controls.description: Enforce the use of strong, approved cryptographic algorithms for all encrypted communications and data storage. Prohibit the use of weak algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, 3DES) and deprecated TLS versions (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, SSLv3).
key_requirements: Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for all encrypted communications
Prohibit SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1
Use AES-128 or AES-256 for symmetric encryption
Prohibit DES, 3DES, RC4, and MD5 for security functions
Apply strong cipher suite configuration to all TLS profiles

controls.name: Incident Detection
controls.objective: Security incidents must be detected in a timely manner through monitoring, alerting, and threat intelligence to minimize dwell time and impact.
controls.description: Deploy monitoring capabilities that generate alerts for security-relevant events. Integrate threat intelligence feeds and configure automated alerting for high-severity events. Threat logs must be reviewed regularly and acted upon within defined SLA.
key_requirements: Generate real-time alerts for high-severity threat events
Monitor threat logs and investigate alerts within defined SLA
Integrate threat intelligence into detection capabilities
Track and document all security incidents
